Quick data point from billing ops: I pulled the tenant invoice windows and matched tokens by route for Acme between 07/22–07/26. Preliminary findings:
- Billing layer shows a legitimate increase in billed token units for three routes: /chat/customer-support, /chat/recommend, /embeddings/summary.
- The increase aligns with a spike in concurrent sessions between 07/24 21:45–23:15 UTC.
- However, console's per-route sampling rate dropped from ~100% to ~10% in that window due to an autosampler backpressure rule firing (we throttle sampling when ingestion queues exceed threshold).

I attached the CSV export Emma sent and my annotated slice in the shared drive. If sampling was reduced, the console explorer will underrepresent the true call counts while tenant billing still counts all tokens — which would explain the mismatch. That points to an instrumentation/sampling policy gap rather than incorrect billing.

Attaching: console-logs-20280725.zip (contains sampling events + ingestion metrics).

1) Short-term: we should send a clear QA note to Acme explaining that sampling backpressure can cause per-route explorer to undercount during ingestion spikes and that billing is based on full token ingestion. Recommend wording (short): "During ingestion spikes, the Console reduces sampling to protect interactive latency; the billing system still records all tokens. We're investigating and will share an action plan." I can draft and Vanessa can send.
2) Medium-term: open an INF engineering ticket to do one of: a) expose the sampler rate/time-series alongside per-route counts, or b) fall back to a lightweight counting path during sampling backpressure so the explorer shows accurate billed volume. Priority: P1 for visibility; P2 for UX polish.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-07-31T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: sudden cost jump in console per-route view — need explanation

Thanks all — engineering triage complete. Summary and plan:

- Root cause: sampler backpressure threshold was hit when ingestion queue latency spiked due to a downstream batching job delay. The sampler intentionally reduces sample rate to keep trace/latency ingestion bounded; it does not affect billing.
- Short-term mitigation (48–72 hours): we will add a visible "sampling_rate" time-series to the per-route explorer and a tooltip that explains billed tokens vs sampled tokens. Low engineering cost: ~3 engineer-days to wire the metric and UI flag. We will also patch the autosampler config to raise the threshold for tenants above enterprise SLA (Acme qualifies) to avoid aggressive downsampling.
- Medium-term (Q3 roadmap): implement a lightweight counting path that emits sampled counters even under backpressure, and add a console mode to "show billed counts" using beaconed metrics. Estimated cost: 3 sprints (frontend + ingestion + backend).

Action items:
- Vanessa: please send Emma the short explanatory note (Lauren's draft below) and confirm we will apply the temporary threshold patch for Acme today.
- Ben: confirm if we should proactively apply the threshold change to other enterprise tenants.
- Lauren: can you open INF-4821 with the high-level spec and acceptance criteria? I've CC'd the ticket link.

I'll attach the sampling event log and a short annotated screenshot once the UI change lands in the canary.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Staff Software Engineer — Ingestion & Telemetry
